channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Suit over fishermen’s deaths in missile strike targets ‘textbook war crime’
item.description: The ACLU filed suit alleging a U.S. missile strike killed two Trinidadian fishermen, arguing sovereign immunity is waived under maritime and human rights law.

item.title: Habeas seen as last chance for justice in felony murder
item.description: A Massachusetts man serving life without parole seeks federal habeas relief after the SJC reinstated a felony murder conviction rooted in shoplifting.

item.title: Bankruptcy filings up 11 percent
item.description: U.S. bankruptcy filings rose 11 percent in 2025, with increases in business and consumer cases, according to new data from the U.S. Courts.

item.title: Boston lawyer honored by crime victims’ community
item.description: Boston lawyer Mitchell Garabedian was recently honored by the National Center for Victims of Crime as the first recipient of the G. Morris Gurley for Justice Award.

item.title: Central Massachusetts’ ‘Legal Luminaries’ celebrated
item.description: Massachusetts Lawyers Weekly recently celebrated the accomplishments of the inaugural class of Legal Luminaries at a special event in Worcester.

item.title: Juvenile justice advocate takes issue with Probation commissioner’s remarks
item.description: Readers respond to a recent story on a reportedly new and improved process for record-sealing at Probation Services.

item.title: A different side to story touting Probation’s speedy process for record-sealing
item.description: Readers respond to a recent story on a reportedly new and improved process for record-sealing at Probation Services.

item.title: Stairwell collapses; injuries result in premature birth
item.description: While using a wooden stairwell at the rear of a third-floor apartment, the plaintiff fell two and a half stories to the ground below when the stairwell collapsed.

item.title: Amputation blamed on improperly placed central line
item.description: On July 9, 2015, the plaintiff, a severely developmentally delayed young man, was found unresponsive at home by his mother. He was immediately taken to the emergency room at a local hospital.

item.title: Trial Court, Appeals Court refuse auditor’s website accessibility audit
item.description: Trial Court and Appeals Court rejected Auditor Diana DiZoglio’s website accessibility audits, citing limits on her authority and an AG opinion.
